items.q: What does print(3 + 4 * 2) show?
items.e: Multiplication happens before addition: 4 * 2 = 8, then 3 + 8.

items.q: What does this print? x = [1, 2, 3]; y = x; y.append(4); print(len(x))
items.e: y and x name the same list, so appending through y changes x too.

items.q: What does [n for n in range(10) if n % 3 == 0] give?
items.e: range(10) starts at 0, and 0 % 3 is 0.

items.q: With d = {"a": 1}, what is d.get("b", 0) + d["a"]?
items.e: .get returns the default 0 for a missing key; d['a'] is 1.

items.q: What does this print? def add(x, items=[]): items.append(x); return items then add(1); print(add(2))
items.e: A default list is created once, when the function is defined, so both calls share it.

items.q: What does this print? g = (n * n for n in range(3)); print(sum(g), sum(g))
items.e: A generator can be used once. The second sum gets nothing left.

items.q: Which command shows the folder you're in?
items.e: pwd prints the working directory.

items.q: What does cd .. do?
items.e: .. means the parent folder.

items.q: What does mkdir -p a/b/c do?
o: Creates a, then b inside it, then c inside that, even if none exist yet
Makes three folders side by side
items.e: -p creates any missing parent folders.

items.q: What does grep -r "TODO" src | wc -l tell you?
o: How many files are in src
How many words are in each TODO
How many lines in the files under src contain TODO
items.e: grep -r searches every file; wc -l counts the matching lines.

items.q: What does python app.py > out.txt 2>&1 do?
o: Sends both normal output and errors into out.txt
Adds to the end of out.txt
Sends output to the file and errors to the screen
items.e: 2>&1 points errors (stream 2) at wherever output (stream 1) is going.

items.q: You run export KEY=abc in one terminal, then open a brand new terminal window and run echo $KEY. What prints?
items.e: export only reaches that shell and programs it starts. A new window starts a fresh shell.

items.q: Which command saves your staged changes into the project's history?
items.e: commit records a snapshot; push only uploads commits.

items.q: What does git add file.py do?
o: Stages the file's changes for the next commit
items.e: add puts changes in the staging area; commit saves them.

items.q: What does git switch -c feature do?
o: Merges feature into the current branch
Creates a branch called feature and moves you onto it
items.e: -c means create.

items.q: You pushed a commit that broke main and your teammates have already pulled it. What's the safest way to undo it?
o: Delete the repository and push again
items.e: revert adds a new commit that undoes the change without rewriting history others already have.

items.q: In a merge conflict, what is between <<<<<<< HEAD and =======?
o: The version on the branch you're on
The version from the branch you're merging in
items.e: HEAD is your current branch.

items.q: On your feature branch you run git rebase main. What happens?
o: All your commits are squashed into one
Your feature commits are replayed on top of the latest main
Your feature branch is merged into main
items.e: Rebase moves your commits so they start from main's tip.

items.q: Which query returns every column of the users table?
items.e: * means every column.

items.q: Which clause keeps only rows where age is over 30?
items.e: WHERE filters rows.

items.q: Which query counts orders per customer?
o: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders ORDER BY customer_id
items.e: GROUP BY makes one row per customer for COUNT to work on.

items.q: What's the difference between WHERE and HAVING?
o: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after
items.e: Use HAVING for conditions on aggregates like SUM or COUNT.

items.q: You LEFT JOIN customers to orders. What happens to customers with no orders?
o: They appear, with NULL in the order columns
items.e: A left join keeps every row from the left table.

items.q: Which keeps one row per customer: their most recent order?
o: SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
Number rows with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) and keep row 1
items.e: A window function ranks each customer's orders separately; LIMIT 1 would return one row in total.

items.q: Which of these is valid JSON?
items.e: JSON needs double quotes around keys and text.

items.q: An API answers with status 404. What does that mean?
items.e: 4xx codes are problems with the request; 404 is a missing resource.

items.q: With Python's requests library, how do you read a JSON response r as a dict?
items.e: r.json() parses the body.

items.q: An API returns 429 Too Many Requests. What should your code do?
o: Wait, then retry with a growing delay
Retry straight away in a loop
items.e: 429 is rate limiting; back off and retry.

items.q: Which HTTP method is meant to be idempotent, so sending it twice has the same effect as once?
o: Only methods that carry a body
items.e: PUT replaces a resource with the same content each time; POST usually creates a new one.

items.q: In FastAPI, @app.get("/items/{id}") handles def item(id: int). What happens on a request to /items/abc?
items.e: Type hints are validated before your function runs.

items.q: What is a Docker container?
o: A type of virtual machine disk
A running instance of an image
items.e: An image is the template; a container is it running.

items.q: Which file describes how to build a Docker image?
items.e: Each Dockerfile line is a build step.

items.q: What does docker run -p 8000:80 app do?
o: Sends port 8000 on your machine to port 80 in the container
Sends container port 8000 to your port 80
Opens both ports to the internet
items.e: The format is host:container.

items.q: Why copy requirements.txt and install packages before COPY . . in a Dockerfile?
o: It always makes the image smaller
It hides your code from the image
So the installed packages stay cached when only your code changes
items.e: Each step is a cached layer; a code change only rebuilds the steps after it.

items.q: Where should an API key go for a deployed container?
o: In an environment variable or secret set on the platform
In a .env file committed to the repo
items.e: Images and repos get shared; secrets set at deploy don't travel with them.

items.q: Your app works on your laptop, but the platform can't reach it. It listens on 127.0.0.1:8000. What fixes it?
o: Open the firewall on your laptop
Listen on 0.0.0.0 and on the port the platform gives you in PORT
items.e: 127.0.0.1 only accepts connections from inside the container itself.

items.q: What does supervised learning need?
o: Examples with the right answers attached
items.e: Labelled data: inputs plus known outputs.

items.q: Why keep a separate test set?
o: To measure how the model does on data it hasn't seen
items.e: Scores on training data flatter the model.

items.q: A fraud model is 99% accurate, and 1% of transactions are fraud. What's the worry?
o: The test set is too big
Saying 'not fraud' every time also scores 99%
items.e: With rare classes, accuracy hides failure; look at precision and recall.

items.q: Training accuracy is 99%, validation accuracy is 70%. What's happening?
items.e: It memorised the training data and doesn't generalise.

items.q: A spam filter must almost never send a real email to spam. Which metric for the spam class matters most?
items.e: Precision is the share of emails flagged as spam that really are spam.

items.q: You scaled features with the mean and standard deviation of the whole dataset, then split it. What's wrong?
o: Test data leaked into training, so scores look better than they are
items.e: Fit the scaler on the training split only.

items.q: What is a token, for a language model?
o: A chunk of text it reads and writes, often part of a word
items.e: Models count and charge by tokens.

items.q: What does lowering the temperature do?
o: Makes answers more predictable and repeatable
items.e: Temperature controls randomness, not truth.

items.q: What is a system prompt for?
o: Instructions and a role that apply to the whole conversation
items.e: It frames every turn that follows.

items.q: What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)?
o: Retraining the model on your documents
Finding relevant documents and putting them in the prompt so the model answers from them
items.e: Retrieval supplies the facts; the model writes the answer.

items.q: Why ask a model for JSON that matches a schema instead of parsing free text?
o: Your code can check it and use it reliably
items.e: Structured output fails loudly instead of quietly.

items.q: How do you know a prompt change made your app better?
o: Ask the model which is better
Check that it uses fewer tokens
Run old and new on the same evaluation set and compare the scores
items.e: One example is an anecdote; a fixed eval set is evidence.
